card.name: Verb after a clinical finding noun
card.fires_on: The verb or auxiliary (was, were, is, remains) right after a clinical finding noun such as hypotension, hyperglycemia or abnormalities. It appears in overdose and case-report text, and is about to be followed by a word like seen, noted or observed.

modes.label: Was/were after finding
modes.description: A past-tense was or were follows a sign or lab abnormality in a case description.
modes.example: No significant hypotension<< was>> apparent at presentation, 18 hours

modes.label: Is/remains after finding
modes.description: A present-tense verb follows a finding in instructions or warnings.
modes.example: If hypotension<< remains>> unresponsive to these conservative measures, consider

modes.label: Partway through finding word
modes.description: The ending of a finding word just before its verb.
modes.example: Significant hyperglyc<<emia>> was seen initially in this patient, but

card.writes: It favors words that report an observation, such as demonstrated or brisk, though the promoted tokens are mixed and not clearly informative.
card.plain: It fires on the small verb after a finding like low blood pressure, just before the text says it was seen or noted.
